beats.text: You spill coffee on your shirt. Now everyone is staring. Right?
Researchers made students wear an embarrassing T-shirt, with a giant picture of Barry Manilow, into a room full of people.
Afterwards, the students guessed about half the room had noticed.
The real number? About a quarter.
Psychologists call it the spotlight effect.
You're the center of your own world. But everyone else is busy being the center of theirs.
So that coffee stain? Most people never even saw it.

sources: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky (2000). The spotlight effect in social judgment: An egocentric bias in estimates of the salience of one's own actions and appearance. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 78(2). Cornell students wore a Barry Manilow T-shirt into a room of peers; they estimated ~46% would notice, actual ~23%.
